focus: what actually blocks an install in the first hour after a publish

registryState.mirrorTarballFor0_1_10: HTTP 302 — the file is served even though the metadata does not list it

installAttempts.why: the mirror lists 0.1.9 as latest, but 0.1.9 was published 02:30 today and is still inside the 24-hour window, so the highest mature version is 0.1.3

correctionToOurOwnHandbook.previousClaim: an exact version spec bypasses minimumReleaseAge, so pinning installs immediately
correctionToOurOwnHandbook.refinedClaim: an exact spec bypasses the release-age window only if the registry's metadata lists that version; a stale mirror rejects it with ERR_PNPM_NO_MATCHING_VERSION even when the tarball is already fetchable
correctionToOurOwnHandbook.practicalWindow: on this machine, for roughly the first hour after a publish, neither the bare name nor the exact pin installs the new version through the bundled pnpm

whatStaysTrue: the market's one-click install delivered a freshly published version earlier tonight, because it resolves against a registry whose metadata already carried it
notMeasured: how long the mirror takes to publish 0.1.10 metadata; the sync request was accepted (201 waiting) and had not landed 42 minutes later
